results.rationale: The cited evidence (Moore 2020, Abu Hureyra) describes meltglass with elevated iridium/platinum/nickel/cobalt at the Younger Dryas boundary in Syria, explicitly read as extending the impact-airburst layer into the Near East/Middle East. This directly supports (not contradicts) the hypothesis's actor, object, place, and mechanism; it is mislabeled as 'refuting' but contains no factual contradiction (e.g., no wrong location, no wrong time period, no denial of meltglass/airburst link). No concrete contradiction found.

All six cited studies (Boslough 2012, Daulton 2010, Haile 2009, Holliday 2014, Paquay 2009, Surovell 2009) report failed replications, absent geochemical signatures, and lack of synchronous extinction/cooling mechanism for the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis — i.e., they substantively support the 'refuted' claim rather than contradict it. Sites/species discussed (e.g., Alaska mammoths/horses, multiple boundary-layer sites) fall within or alongside North America, consistent with the stated place. No concrete contradiction found despite being listed under 'refuting evidence'.
